text:
Matt S.: Hey team — BrightLayer is doing a live 3-day POC next week and asked for a temporary bump to support a demo spike. Current hosted key is 50 QPS, they want ~500 QPS for 72 hours. Can we approve a short window?
Tara L.: 500 QPS for 72h — got it. A couple quick Qs: is this for a single API key / project? Will they use streaming endpoints or short-completion calls? Any compliance constraints?
Matt S.: Single project/key. Mostly short completions (interactive UI, ~1.5s responses). They’ll route ~95% through our API, small % embedding calls. No special compliance beyond standard SOC2; they asked for audit logs.
Jeff P.: For hosted we have a few options: 1) temporary quota increase on their hosted API key (fast, lowest friction) — risk: could affect other tenants if misused; we should scope to key + per-route caps, and enable stricter throttling backoffs. 2) spin up a short-lived Dedicated pool for the POC (more isolation, predictable latency) — requires capacity slot and billing approval. 3) suggest client do synthetic load during demo using parallel clients + batching to simulate QPS while keeping actual production traffic lower.
Tara L.: Also important: pricing. If we permit 10x QPS, we should lock a flat day-rate or estimate tokens and add a temporary commit. Sales, do we want to offer a promo credit for the spike or bill on usage?
Matt S.: They prefer not to be billed mid-demo. Could we offer a 3-day trial credit that covers expected usage and re-evaluate after?
Jeff P.: Ops: we can provision a scoped temporary key with per-route rate caps and a TTL. Example policy: 

```
{
  "key": "scoped-demo-BrightLayer",
  "qps": 500,
  "routes": {
    "/v1/complete": 450,
    "/v1/embeddings": 50
  },
  "expires_at": "2026-04-08T18:00:00Z"
}
```

That would limit blast radius. We also add automatic rollback at TTL and notify if sustained error rates > 5%. Need infra approval to raise the global per-tenant throttle for that key.
Nina (support): Security note: customer asked for proof of data handling + audit logs during demo. We can enable request-level logging and share anonymized logs. Also confirm whether they want a scoped key that cannot access SSO-protected routes.
Matt S.: They want logs showing request IDs and latencies for demo. Scoped key is fine. No SSO for the demo.
Tara L.: Action items: - Jeff, can you open the quota ticket and indicate Dedicated vs Hosted path? - Nina, prepare the audit log export template (anonymized). - Matt, confirm if they want us to run load tests or if they'll drive it.
Jeff P.: Opening ticket now. Ticket #Q-89271 created for temporary hosted quota increase and scoped key provisioning. @quota-bot will post updates. I flagged dedicated option if we hit infra limits. ETA: 24h for hosted-scoped key, 48–72h if we need dedicated pool.
quota-bot: Auto: Created request Q-89271. Current status: pending-review by infra. Please attach expected RPS profile and start/end window.
Matt S.: I'll send the exact start/end times + expected token estimate to the ticket. Also we should draft a short customer-facing doc: "What to expect during demo — rate limits, retries, and token consumption".
Tara L.: Good. For pricing: propose a small demo credit equal to projected max cost; finance check later. Sales to confirm in the ticket.
Nina (support): I'll attach sample logs and a short note on anonymization. Also will include steps to rotate the scoped key post-demo.
Matt S.: Thanks all, will update BrightLayer and post the start time once ticket approved. :thumbsup:
